_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who are dependent on parenteral support

pivotal_trials.trial_name: CL-0600-020 (Study 020), the pivotal adequate and well-controlled study
pivotal_trials.design: 24-week multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to placebo or teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with Short Bowel Syndrome who are dependent on parenteral nutrition/IV fluids
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Binary Response: number and percentage of subjects achieving at least a 20% reduction from baseline in weekly PN volume at Week 20 sustained through Week 24

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) across all studies (n=566): abdominal pain (30.0%), injection site reactions (22.4%), nausea (18.2%), headaches (15.9%), abdominal distension (13.8%), upper respiratory tract infection (11.8%). Serious risks based on mechanism of action include possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhanced colorectal polyp growth, intestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disease.
target_moa: A recombinant analog of human glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2); a GLP-2 receptor agonist that promotes growth and repair of intestinal epithelium (increased villus height and crypt depth), improving intestinal absorption

rems.type: A REMS is required consisting of a communication plan and elements to assure safe use to mitigate the risk of possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhancement of colon polyp growth, gastrointestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disorders.

advisory_committee.vote: Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee (GIDAC) met October 16, 2012; voted unanimously 12 YES, 0 NO that a clinically meaningful benefit was demonstrated in adult SBS patients.

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with Short Bowel Syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the expansion of the indication to pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who are dependent on parenteral support, and proposes modifications to the approved GATTEX (teduglutide) Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS).

orphan_indication.text: US Orphan Drug designation granted June 29, 2000 for the recombinant human GLP-2 formulation for subcutaneous use in SBS.

summary.text: GATTEX (teduglutide) received an orphan drug designation (granted June 29, 2000) and was reviewed under a standard review designation. It was approved first cycle for adult SBS with a required REMS and a required postmarketing registry study.

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for GATTEX (teduglutide [rDNA origin]) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhancement of colon polyp growth, gastrointestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disorders associated with GATTEX (teduglutide [rDNA origin]).

requirement.text: 1978-1: A prospective, multi-center, long-term observational registry study of SBS patients treated with teduglutide to assess long-term safety and rule out a clinically meaningful increase in colorectal cancer risk; patients enrolled over 5 years and followed at least 10 years.

citations.quote: 1978-1 A prospective, multi-center, long-term, observational, registry study, of short bowel syndrome patients treated with teduglutide in a routine clinical setting, to assess the long-term safety of teduglutide. Design the study around a testable hypothesis to rule out a clinically meaningful increase in colorectal cancer risk above an estimated background risk in a suitable comparator.
Patients should be enrolled over an initial 5-year period and then followed for a period of at least 10 years from the time of enrollment.

requirement.text: 1978-2: Elemental impurities specifications will be expanded to include limits and testing for all metals, as recommended in USP <232>.
